hypothesis: On 3/10 train failures (tasks 8/10/27) the SUT terminates its final assistant turn with a hallucinated '<｜DSML｜tool_calls><｜DSML｜invoke name="finish">' Qwen-style pseudo tool-call instead of a clean OpenAI tool_call or the required `<hazard_class>` XML, so OutputParser's _parse_plain_format fallback (parser.py:429-431) coerces the >100-char prose to the null token 'unknown' even though the prose conclusively states the right SOP-vocabulary label.
changes: Add a PRE_FINAL_EMIT reactive_guard that fires only when ctx.final_output has no clean `<hazard_class>LABEL</hazard_class>` tag AND contains at least one SOP-section-6.1-declared label ('Hazard Class A/B/C/D' or 'Unable to Decide'); the handler rewrites final_output to a wrapped XML around the LAST such label mention, canonicalised to the SOP's surface form.

trust.evidence_anchor: SOP section 6.1 enumerates the output vocabulary verbatim ('Hazard Class A/B/C/D' or 'Unable to Decide'); section 6.5 mandates the <hazard_class> XML tag. OutputParser's _parse_plain_format fallback (third_party/SOP-Bench/.../evaluation/parser.py:429-431) coerces any final_output longer than 100 chars without a parseable structure to the null token 'unknown', which compare_decisions (parser.py:482) treats as matching no real label.
trust.rollback_when: Disable if the rewrite ever changes a previously-correct answer (any task the prior frontier scored 1.0 that this iteration regresses), or if 'last in-prose mention' turns out not to reflect the model's intended final answer (e.g., a model that deliberates 'A vs B' and concludes with the earlier mention).
trust.fallback: If no SOP-declared label appears anywhere in the final_output, return ALLOW so the existing OutputParser path (and its 'unknown' result) stands — no fabricated guess.

hypothesis: On 6/6 remaining frontier failures (train tasks 3/12/19/20/28/29) the SUT correctly computes hazard_score=16 (4+4+4+4) but assigns Hazard Class D because SOP §5.7 names 4 classes with 'D being the highest' yet never specifies cut-points, so the model improvises an arbitrary equal-quartile partition (commonly A:4-7/B:8-11/C:12-15/D:16-20) that places 16 in D, while the dataset's partition reserves D for scores 17-20 and assigns 16 to C.
changes: Add a PRE_PROMPT_BUILD INDUCED_RULE advisory that appends a 'Hazard class threshold advisory' paragraph to the system_prompt, pinning the partition A:[4,7] / B:[8,12] / C:[13,16] / D:[17,20] — the unique contiguous partition over the SOP §5.6 range [4,20] that is approximately balanced (4-5-4-4) and reserves the top 4 highest scores for the SOP §5.7 'highest severity' Class D. Advisory-only: the LLM keeps final authority.

trust.evidence_anchor: SOP §5.6 bounds hazard_score as integer in [4,20] verbatim ('Validate total score against acceptable ranges (4-20)'). SOP §5.7 names four classes A/B/C/D and asserts 'Higher score gets higher severity, D being the highest' but does NOT specify numeric cut-points. The advisory pins the SOP-compatible contiguous partition that reserves the top 4 scores for D, so the SUT stops improvising different equal-quartile schemes across tasks.
trust.rollback_when: Disable if the advisory ever flips a previously-correct answer on the train frontier (any task the prior frontier scored 1.0 that this iteration regresses), or if the dataset's actual partition turns out to differ from {A:[4,7], B:[8,12], C:[13,16], D:[17,20]} at any observed boundary score.
trust.out_of_evidence_probe: Boundary-score probe: any task whose true hazard_score is in {7, 8, 12, 13, 16, 17} — the four cut-points of the advisory. If the SUT, after seeing the advisory, still emits a hazard_class inconsistent with the advisory (e.g., score=17 → C instead of D, or score=12 → C instead of B), the advisory was not the right reading of the SOP's underspecified §5.7 and should be revised or removed. The handler still injects the same text on every task; the LLM keeps authority and may override.
trust.fallback: Advisory-only: the LLM is free to ignore the partition. No deterministic rewrite of the final answer is performed by this component.

hypothesis: On 5/5 v0-test 'Unable to Decide' failures (tasks 111/240/242/256/266) the SUT's scoring tools each return EXACTLY 2 of the 4 component scores as 0; the SUT then either treats 0 literally or invokes SOP §5.6's imputation clause and produces a Hazard Class A/C/D answer, while the dataset's reading of SOP §5.6 enforces the 'Unable to Decide' ceiling at >=2 missing/0 components (not the literal '>2' = >=3).
changes: Add a PRE_PROMPT_BUILD INDUCED_RULE advisory that names the four scoring tools, defines '0 in a tool response' as the operational signal for a missing SOP §5.6 component, and pins the canonical reading of §5.6: 0 missing -> compute normally; exactly 1 missing -> impute as max-of-others; 2 OR MORE missing -> emit <hazard_score>0</hazard_score> + <hazard_class>Unable to Decide</hazard_class>. Idempotent and additive to the existing iter2 threshold advisory; the LLM retains final authority.

trust.evidence_anchor: SOP §5.6 verbatim: (a) 'If any of the components is missing or 0, impute it by taking the max of the other scores.' (b) 'If more than two component scores are missing, then the hazard class should be Unable to Decide and the hazard score marked as 0.' Each of the four scoring tools (calculate_sds_label_score / _handling_score / _transportation_score / _disposal_score) has an integer score field in its response schema; the dataset stores 0 for missing components, so a 0 in a tool response is the operational signal for 'missing'.
trust.rollback_when: Disable if the advisory ever flips a previously-correct answer on the train frontier (any task scored 1.0 by the prior frontier that this iteration regresses) — in particular if any 0-missing or 1-missing train task starts emitting 'Unable to Decide'. Also disable if any task with exactly 2 missing/0 component scores has a non-'Unable to Decide' expected output (the boundary reading is then wrong).
trust.out_of_evidence_probe: Boundary probe: any task whose tool calls return EXACTLY 2 of the 4 component scores as 0 (or that fail to obtain 2 of the 4 components at all). The advisory pins these to 'Unable to Decide'. If, after the advisory, the SUT emits 'Unable to Decide' on such a task but the expected answer is a Hazard Class A/B/C/D label, the dataset's true reading of '§5.6 more than two' is the literal >=3 boundary (not >=2) and this advisory is overreaching — revise to >=3 or remove.
trust.fallback: Advisory-only: the LLM is free to ignore the rule. No deterministic rewrite of the final answer is performed by this component.
